requirements_summary: Workloads: real-time chat + scoring (low-latency) and nightly reranking/embeddings (throughput-focused)
Latency targets: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 80ms, p99 <= 120ms for chat under declared concurrency
Throughput targets: sustain 45 tokens/sec per session for 3k concurrent sessions; burst capability to 80k tokens/sec for short windows
Capacity planning: reserve baseline 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) with autoscale up to +50% for market open; cold-start scale-up < 90s desired, warm-pool approach preferred
Autoscaling policy needs: scale-up based on queue length + input-rate, scale-down guardrails to avoid thrash, warm-pool minimum nodes, pre-warm heuristics tied to business hours
Queueing behavior: deterministic FIFO preferred for scoring; want priority queues for risk-critical requests and backpressure signals to caller rather than silent throttling
SLA asks: performance credits for missed p99, contractual throughput guarantees, scheduled maintenance windows with advance notices
Observability: real-time per-route token rate, tail-latency alerts, exportable traces, cost per-token accounting
poc_findings: Steady-state throughput met expectations for chat and reranking when pool warm.
Cold scale-ups introduced 4-6s latency cliffs for some long-context prompts — root cause: worker initialization + large KV cache population.
Suggested mitigations: maintain a small hot pool of GPU workers with preloaded model weights and KV-prime routines; implement prioritized warm-up for risk-critical routes.
Batching trade-offs: larger batches improve throughput but increase tail for single-request response; recommend per-route batching configs.
Quantization: safe to use for embeddings/reranking; for core scoring models want FP16/AMP with tuned kernels to preserve accuracy.
